hero_title: The Git-based CMS built for static site generators
hero_description: Giving everyone a voice to speak. A lightweight cms and Git backed headless content workspace for sharing experiences over the web with zero friction.
features_headline: A friendly, open source Git based CMS for static sites.
feature_content_creation_desc: Craft and edit posts with an intuitive, distraction free Markdown editor equipped with rich formatting and live syntax highlighting. Write at the speed of thought using natural language solutions powered by Wit.ai or OpenAI Whisper-compatible models.
feature_git_desc: LightCMS embraces the modern Jamstack workflow by keeping all content in standard frontmatter schema based Markdown files. Leverage Git's versioning and pull requests to collaborate transparently with complete history, zero vendor lock-in, and no database maintenance.
feature_eco_title: Eco friendly delivery for blogs & documentation
feature_eco_desc: Pre rendered static sites consume significantly less energy than database driven apps which fetch data from a server every time a page is loaded. Whether you are publishing an engineering blog or maintaining enterprise project documentation, deploy across edge CDNs with unmatched speed and a minimal carbon footprint.
feature_templates_title: Multiple templates for static site generators
feature_templates_desc: Get started quickly with ready made, handcrafted templates for popular Static Site Generators (SSGs) like Hugo, Astro, and Zola. You can save time using these pre built configurations or use the LLM to customize any template to perfectly fit your static site needs.
feature_copilot_desc: Leverage AI copilot to aid your content writing experience.
about_title: A Git-based headless CMS that stays out of your way
about_subtitle: Built with SvelteKit, TypeScript, and viteplus
about_p1: LightCMS is a Git-based content workspace for people who want to publish writing, not babysit infrastructure. It pairs a fast, distraction-free editor with storage you already own: every post is a Markdown file with frontmatter, committed to your own repository, reviewed like any other change, and deployed by the pipeline you already trust.
about_why_p1: Most publishing tools ask you to trade ownership for convenience. Your words end up in someone else's database, behind someone else's login, exported — if you're lucky — through someone else's format. LightCMS takes the opposite position: the editor is the product, the content stays yours.
about_why_p2: The goal is to close the gap between people who have something worth sharing and the complexity that normally stands in the way. You shouldn't need to understand rebase flags, Markdown linters, frontmatter validators or GitHub token scopes to publish three paragraphs. And you shouldn't hand your archive to a platform to avoid learning them.
about_ssg_title: Works with the static site generator you already use
about_ssg_p1: If your SSG reads frontmatter, LightCMS is a companion to it — Hugo, Astro, Zola, Jekyll, Eleventy, SvelteKit, and anything else in that family. Content is stored as plain Markdown files with a structured frontmatter schema, so nothing is smuggled in a proprietary format. Ready-made templates get you from empty repository to published site quickly, and you can hand any template to an LLM and reshape it.
about_jamstack_p1: Pages are prerendered and served from an edge CDN. There is no database answering a query per visitor and no application server idling between requests. That means faster pages for readers, nothing to patch for you, and a fraction of the energy a database-driven site burns. Read more in
about_jamstack_link: Static Sites and CO2: Building a Greener Web
about_version_title: Version history, not a revision guess
about_version_p1: Every publish is a commit. You get a reviewable diff, an author, a timestamp, and a rollback that actually reverts. Collaborate through pull requests instead of shared passwords, and clone the repository at any time — there is no export step, because there is nothing to export it from.
about_opensource_p1: LightCMS is built with SvelteKit, TypeScript and Vite, released as open source. Run it hosted, or follow the
about_opensource_p2: to deploy your own instance with your own GitHub App, PostgreSQL database and optional AI endpoints.
